findings.summary: In the mixed case, M18.239 rewrites a pack's entry as a 1.0 envelope and drops every earlier definition of an unknown used type that is not a valid 1.0 definition. Before the change, the old code kept the earlier entry whole in that case. So a file from a newer host whose entry holds a 1.1-only definition loses that type when saved by this host, whenever this host knows one other type of the pack. The acceptance says 'an earlier refused entry's types are not lost'. The row's own test asserts the loss ('lines:bad' from a 1.1 envelope is not carried). ADR-0048's amendment says such a definition 'is dropped, since it would make the whole entry refused' but does not say this reverses M18.112's keep-whole behaviour, and nothing logs the dropped ids.
findings.evidence: connector-entries.ts:76-86 packEntry returns entryOf([...known, ...carried(earlier, unknown, pack)]) whenever known.length > 0. carried (:57-68) keeps only `registrable` definitions (parseConnectorDefs on a 1.0 envelope plus describeOf). The old code at 6c5a7f0^ was `if (known.length === defs.length) out.set(name, ...) else if (earlier !== undefined) out.set(name, earlier)`. connector-entries.test.ts (6c5a7f0) builds an earlier entry with formatVersion '1.1' holding { id: 'lines:bad', router: 'orthogonal', decoration: { kind: 'none-such' } }, a used type, and expects it absent ('bad not 1.0'). M18.239 acceptance: '... merged with any earlier entry's definitions of the unknown types, so that ... an earlier refused entry's types are not lost'.
findings.failure_scenario: A pack ships a 1.1 decoration in a later Fluxion. A person opens such a file in this version, which has the pack's older types, and saves it. The 1.1 type's definition is gone from connectors/<pack>.json, so a newer reader without the pack draws those connectors plain. Nobody is told, and the loss cannot be recovered from the file.

findings.summary: M18.216 closed with its two review minors open, and one of them is a clause of the row. The acceptance says 'WHEN reading one first-party pack index or category rejects THE SYSTEM SHALL list that pack under the catalog's refused packs'. A rejected category read is instead reported per shape through documentCatalog's onProblem and never listed under refused, because categories load lazily after the refused list is built. The design is reasonable, but the row text was not changed through spec. The hook's rejection branch, the only code that makes 'no unhandled rejection' true in the studio, has no test.
findings.evidence: 1cfbea5 body: 'Review r1 pass with two minors left open: the hook's rejection handler has no test, and a failed category read is reported per shape rather than listed under refused (categories load lazily).' pack-catalog.test.ts (1cfbea5), category case: `expect(problems).toEqual([expect.stringContaining('The shape devices:laptop could not be loaded: category could not be read')])`, with no check of catalog.refused. use-document-catalog.ts:17-25 adds the second .then argument that logs 'the first-party packs could not be read'. No test file references useDocumentCatalog's rejection (`git grep -n 'could not be read' apps/studio/src/*.test.*` matches only pack-catalog.test.ts's category message). M18.216 is done at 1cfbea5.
findings.failure_scenario: A later refactor of useDocumentCatalog drops the rejection handler, for example by going back to `void bundledPackCatalog(...).then(...)`. An offline studio then raises an unhandled rejection again, and no test fails. Separately, a checker of the row's text finds a category failure missing from refused and reopens a done row.
